messages:
Sam: Heads-up — we're seeing a surge of GPU attach failures in us-west2 after last night's nvme firmware push. node-provisioner shows attach stuck at 'waiting for scratch' and kube attach timeouts. 15% of pending GPU jobs are failing to schedule.

Lena: ugh, any obvious io metrics?

Sam: yes — nvme write latency jumped and iops saturation on ephemeral scratch. quick tail of the node logs:
```
May 01 03:12:07 node-uw2-17 kubelet: attach request -> waiting for /dev/nvme0n1: io wait 98%
May 01 03:12:09 kernel: nvme0: I/O wait surge, rc=-5
May 01 03:12:10 janitor[pid]: scrub started concurrency=12
```

Ajay: @Lena @Sam this sounds like the janitor/scrub job ramped and tripped some firmware path on that nvme cohort. we've seen similar on older firmware where concurrent trim+fsync bursts stall device scheduling.

Marta: Confirmed correlation with scrub logs — nightly scrub ramped at 03:10 and concurrency was 12. IOPS heatmap shows scrub writes overlapping with GPU attach window for about 4 zones.

Sam: metrics snapshot:
- scratch iops baseline 10k -> peaked 85k
- avg write latency 0.8ms -> 25ms
- gpu attach median latency 120ms -> 2.3s and timeouts

Lena: can we throttle janitor immediately? Velcro-scheduler can avoid nodes with high nvme_io_wait if we tag them. Workaround: reduce scrub concurrency, add a temporary taint to nodes, and avoid scheduling attaches during the ramp window.

Ajay: Agreed. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) reduce nightly scrub concurrency from 12 -> 2 (hotfix) 2) add node-label scratch-io:degraded so provisioner doesn't pick them 3) bump attach timeout to 10s for retry loop. I can push the scrub throttling patch now.

Sam: please push. I'll flip the label and add a k8s admission filter to prefer other AZs for GPU attaches.

Marta: Quick note on cost/ops tradeoff — lowering scrub concurrency will increase time-to-clean by ~6 hours which raises wear backlog; long-term we'd prefer firmware rollback or patch from vendor. But for now throttle + label is safest.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-318 — us-west2 gpu attach failures due to scratch nvme iops surge. Pager duty notified.

Lena: Thanks. After hotfix we should monitor attach success rate and nvme SMART counters for CRC errors. If we see increasing reallocated sectors we may need to retire cohorts.

Ajay: Hotfix applied: scrub concurrency set to 2 in job config; nodes in us-west2 labeled scratch-io=degraded. Attaching retries increased. Initial attach success up from 62% -> 94% in last 15m.

Sam: Nice work. We'll keep the label for 2 maintenance windows and schedule a vendor firmware review. :thumbsup:
